newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco in talks on sale of Samir refinery.
newsitem.headline: Morocco in talks on sale of Samir refinery.

text.p: Morocco, which expects up to $0.5 billion from the privatisation of a majority stake of Samir oil refinery, said on Monday talks are underway with four oil groups to form a hard core of investors.
Societe Marocaine de Raffinage (Samir) is Morocco's main oil refinery and holds 80 percent of refined products market share.
"At this stage we are in discussion with four oil groups to set up Samir's hard core of investors," Privatisation Minister Abderrahman Saaidi told Reuters.
Saaidi declined to give details on the groups involved in the final discussion with the Moroccan authorities for the sale of more than 51 percent of the refinery stock.
A Casablanca-based stockbroker told Reuters Royal Dutch/Shell was interested in the project but it was not known how much it offered to purchased the refinery's privatised stock.

The privatisation ministry floated 30 percent of the state-owned Samir stock on the bourse at $310 million in March 1996. It also promised to sell up to 51 pecent by end December 1996 but nothing has been done since, a market analyst said.
Located on the Atlantic coast at Mohammedia near the financial city of Casablanca, Samir has a capacity of 6.0 million tonnes a year.
One of the 47 listed stocks on the bourse, it was last traded at 287 dirhams per share, brokers said.
